{{also|Appendix:Variations of "con"}}
==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|com-}}
* [[cor-#English|cor-]] ''([[prerhotic]])''
* [[Ꝯ]]

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˌkən/|/ˈkʌn/|/ˌkɑːn/|/ˈkɒn/}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=with|:inh|enm:con-|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|con-}}, from {{der|en|la|con-}}, from {{m|la|cum|t=with}}.

====Prefix====
{{en-prefix}}

# {{senseid|en|unite}} [[unite|Unite]]: to unite into a collection indicated by the root word.
#: {{uxi|en|[[concorporate|'''con'''corporate]]}} is united into a single body, {{uxi|en|[[conglobulate|'''con'''globulate]]}} is to collect together into a globule, {{uxi|en|[[conglutination|'''con'''glutination]]}} is to glue together into a glutination
# {{senseid|en|together}} [[together|Together]]: the root is done together.
#: {{uxi|en|[[conarticular|'''con'''articular]]}} is that articulates together, {{uxi|en|[[conjubilant|'''con'''jubilant]]}} is rejoicing together, {{uxi|en|[[consubsistence|'''con'''subsistence]]}} is subsistence together
# {{senseid|en|commonality}} Having [[commonality]], having the same property indicated by the root.
#: {{uxi|en|[[confocal|'''con'''focal]]}} is having the same foci, {{uxi|en|[[consimilar|'''con'''similar]]}} is having similarities in common, {{uxi|en|[[conterminant|'''con'''terminant]]}} is having the same termination
## {{senseid|en|belonging}} [[belonging|Belonging]] to the same group indicated by the root.
##: {{uxi|en|[[confamilial|'''con'''familial]]}} is belonging to the same taxonomic family, {{uxi|en|[[contypic|'''con'''typic]]}} is relating to the same type, {{uxi|en|[[conspecific|'''con'''specific]]}} is relating to the same species
## {{senseid|en|synchronous}} [[synchronous|Synchronous]] or [[simultaneous]] with the root.
##: {{uxi|en|[[connascent|'''con'''nascent]]}} is born together, {{uxi|en|[[concreate|'''con'''create]]}} is to create at the same time, {{uxi|en|[[congeneration|'''con'''generation]]}} is simultaneous generation (as of heat and light from the same action)
## {{senseid|en|fellow}} A [[fellow]] kind of the root.
##: {{uxi|en|[[concitizen|'''con'''citizen]]}} is a fellow citizen, {{uxi|en|[[condisciple|'''con'''disciple]]}} is a fellow disciple, {{uxi|en|[[concelebrant|'''con'''celebrant]]}} is one who concelebrates
# {{senseid|en|doing}} To do the root.
#: {{uxi|en|[[convivify|'''con'''vivify]]}} is to gain eternal life, {{uxi|en|[[confix|'''con'''fix]]}} is to make firm, {{uxi|en|[[constrict|'''con'''strict]]}} is to limit or restrict
## {{senseid|en|intensifying}} [[intensifying|Intensifying]] the root.
##: {{uxi|en|[[congenial|'''con'''genial]]}} is very genial, {{uxi|en|[[connatural|'''con'''natural]]}} is inherent (very natural), {{uxi|en|[[convicinity|'''con'''vicinity]]}} is immediate vicinity (very close)
# Indicating a common origin:
## {{senseid|en|with}} Found [[with]]. What is found with the root.
##: {{uxi|en|[[consalazinic acid|'''con'''salazinic acid]]}} is a lichen acid found together with salazinic acid, {{uxi|en|[[conphaseolin|'''con'''phaseolin]]}} is a protein found with phaseolin, {{uxi|en|[[connegative|'''con'''negative]]}} is a verb form used with a negative verb in certain languages
## {{senseid|en|from}} [[from|From]], coming from the root.
##: {{uxi|en|[[consequence|'''con'''sequence]]}} as what comes from the sequence, {{uxi|en|[[convicine|'''con'''vicine]]}} is a glycoside coming from vicine, {{uxi|en|[[connatal|'''con'''natal]]}} is an anomaly present at birth
# {{senseid|en|internal}} When one entity is put into another, or one entity affects the other.
#: {{uxi|en|[[conplastic|'''con'''plastic]]}} is produced by introducing the genetic material from one strain into the cytoplasm of another; {{uxi|en|[[contour|'''con'''tour]]}} is a speech sound which behaves as a single segment, but which makes an internal transition from one quality, place, or manner to another; {{uxi|en|[[converb|'''con'''verb]]}} is a verb with a stressed, separable prefix
# {{senseid|en|mutually}} [[mutuality|Mutuality]], indicating a reciprocal relationship or influence
#: {{uxi|en|[[confraternization|'''con'''fraternization]]}} is mutual fraternization, {{uxi|en|[[confated|'''con'''fated]]}} is fated with something else, {{uxi|en|[[connascence|'''con'''nascence]]}} is a relationship between two or more elements of software in which changing one necessitates changing the others in order to maintain overall correctness
# {{senseid|en|surround}} To [[surround]] or [[adorn]] with
#: {{uxi|en|[[constrict|'''con'''strict]]}} is to coil around prey in order to asphyxiate it, {{uxi|en|[[constellate|'''con'''stellate]]}} is to adorn with constellations
# {{senseid|en|uniform}} [[uniform|Uniform]], or made to be the same as.
#: {{uxi|en|[[concolorate|'''con'''colorate]]}} is having a uniform colour

=====Usage notes=====
{{m|en||Con-}} becomes
: {{m|en|col-}} before ''l'': {{m|en|collaborate}};
: {{m|en|com-}} before ''b'', ''m'', and ''p'': {{m|en|combat}}, {{m|en|commit}}, {{m|en|compel}};
: {{m|en|cor-}} before ''r'': {{m|en|correlation}};
It can also appear as {{m|en|co-}} before a vowel: {{m|en|coexistence}}, {{m|en|cosine}}.

=====Synonyms=====
* {{sense|together}} {{l|en|co-}}, {{l|en|com-}}/{{l|en|col-}}/{{l|en|cor-}}, {{l|en|syn-}}/{{l|en|syl-}}/{{l|en|sym-}}, {{l|en|inter-}}

* Danish: {{t|da|kon-}}, {{t|da|sam-}}
* French: {{t+|fr|con-}}
* German: {{t+|de|kon-}}, {{t+|de|mit-}}
* Middle English: {{t|enm|con-}}
* Norwegian:
*: Bokmål: {{t|nb|kon-}}, {{t+|nb|sam-}}
*: Nynorsk: {{t|nn|kon-}}
* Old Norse: {{t|non|sam-}}
* Swedish: {{t+|sv|kon-}}, {{t+|sv|sam-}}
{{trans-bottom}}

==Latin==
{{wikidata lexeme|L35197}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|la|id=bringing together|:inh|itc-pro:*kom-<id:with>|tree=1}}
{{inh+|la|itc-pro|*kom-}}. Related to the preposition {{m|la|cum|t=with}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{la-IPA}}

===Prefix===
{{head|la|prefix}}

# {{n-g|Used in compounds to indicate a being or bringing together of several objects}}
#: {{m|la|coeo|'''co'''eō}}, {{m|la|colloquor|'''col'''loquor}}, {{m|la|convivor|'''con'''vīvor}}, etc.: {{m|la|colligo|'''col'''ligō}}, {{m|la|compono|'''com'''pōnō}}, {{m|la|condo|'''con'''dō}}, etc.
# {{n-g|Used in compounds to indicate the completeness, perfecting of any act, and thus gives intensity to the signification of the simple word}}
#: {{m|la|commaculo|'''com'''maculō}}, {{m|la|commendo|'''com'''mendō}}, {{m|la|concito|'''con'''citō}}, {{m|la|comminuo|'''com'''minuō}}, {{m|la|concerpo|'''con'''cerpō}}, {{m|la|concido|'''con'''cīdō}}, {{m|la|convello|'''con'''vellō}}, etc.

====Usage notes====
* Before vowel phonemes and ''h'', the prefix becomes {{m|la|co-}}, or rarely {{m|la|com-}}; this does not include ''i'' used as ''j'' or ''u'' used as ''v''.
* Before ''b'', ''m'' and ''p'', the prefix may become {{m|la|com-}}.
* Before ''l'', the prefix may become {{m|la|col-}}.
* Before ''r'', the prefix may become {{m|la|cor-}}.
* Before ''n'', the prefix becomes {{m|la|cō-}} (or remains {{m|la||con-}}, in [[Late Latin]]).
* Before original ''gn'', the prefix becomes {{m|la|co-}} and ''gn'' is not reduced to ''n''.

As usual in Latin phonology, the sequences ''ons'' and ''onf'' are pronounced with nasalised long vowels, and the vowel is written with a macron, i.e., {{m|la|cōnspīrō}} and {{m|la|cōnferō}}.
